N2.3.heard: He also passed on something a local official had said to him that night.

N2.4.heard: Then, he spoke directly to the families.

N2.5.heard: Asked what should be done, he said the facts had to come first.

N3.a.heard: The governor's charge to the commission was to identify the lessons the Columbine taught.

N3.b.heard: It's stated hope was that even one life could be saved by effective law enforcement and rescue responses to a future emergency.

N3.c.heard: The report explains why SWAT teams act together. They train as teams, typically 20 hours a month, so that each member knows what the others will do.

N3.d.heard: The commission also stressed that the situation was extremely chaotic. Witness after witness told that the Columbine was unlike any other tragedy they had ever experienced.

N3.e.heard: That training, it said, should reach every officer who might be a first responder, and every school resource officer whether or not they serve on a SWAT team.

N3.f.heard: It also asked for much more training in incident command, so that command officers can take charge at the beginning of a crisis and communicate their objectives clearly.

N3.g.heard: A threat assessment team, it said, should include a school staff member who knows the students, such as a counselor or a vice principal.

N3.h.heard: If possible, it should also include a mental health professional and someone with a law enforcement background.

N3.i.heard: Every report of a verbal or written threat it said should be taken seriously by the team.

N3.k.heard: and students should learn about the anonymous reporting line and be told why it matters to their safety.

N3.j.heard: It also urged every school to adopt a bullying prevention program that has already been tested and proven effective.

N3.l.heard: The president had spoken of early warning signs on the night of the attack, too

N4.6a.heard: His advice to communities that night was to study what lessons could be learned.

4.3.heard: In 2002, Texas State University, the San Marcos Police Department, and the Hayes County Sheriff's Office formed a training center called Alert.
